name: Bright Data Browser API

modes.label: Bandwidth-billed browser
modes.note: Billed only on GB of traffic through the browser; no instance/time charge (do not interpret as a free compute VM). Same rate in every country; premium domains cost more per GB (rate not published). One target domain per session; 60-min max session; 5-min idle timeout; 30 s client connect timeout. Unspecified guest OS is not a selectable OS guarantee.

plans.name: Free tier
plans.note: 5,000 credits/month (~$7.50), shared pool across Unlocker/SERP/Scraper/Studio/Browser API; Browser API at 5 credits per MB (~1 GB); reset on the 1st, no rollover; hard stop without funds; not issued on custom PAYG or pre-commit plans; unfunded accounts limited to 1,000 req/min on SERP/Unlocker/proxy.

plans.name: Pay as you go
plans.note: $8/GB from a pre-paid wallet (you deposit funds; auto-recharge optional when balance < 85%). No monthly commitment; unlimited concurrent sessions.

plans.name: Scale $499
plans.note: 71 GB included; $7/GB rate in page slider data.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Custom package, SLA, SSO, audit logs.

features.ip_note: All traffic billed $8/GB pay-as-you-go (Scale $499/mo incl. 71 GB) with built-in residential proxy rotation and unlocking included.

caveats: Storage, snapshot GiB-month and public IPv4 prices are not published in the reviewed sources; null is not free.

No guaranteed vCPU allocation published; browser-hour is not a verified 4-vCPU/8-GiB VM equivalent. The sizes card keeps unknown hardware null; do not coerce it to zero or auto-rank against resource-guaranteed VMs.
Browser RAM is not published unless a specific mode overrides it.

Rendered currency widgets returned empty prices; exact USD recovered from public data-usd and data-tiers attributes in saved HTML. These are primary-page values, not guessed from the headline from-$5/GB.

Network meters browser/proxy traffic, not necessarily customer-facing VM egress. Plans have different GB pricing; strict engine cannot couple mode-specific network rates with package allowances. Card network remains null, and GB tariffs stay in raw/regime data.
Unlimited concurrency is a marketing entitlement, not verified load testing. Session lifetime/profile retention, CPU/RAM, resolution and separate recording prices remain unverified.
First-deposit match: Bright Data matches a first deposit dollar-for-dollar up to $500; matched credits expire after 90 days and need >= $5/month usage. Not modelled.

fleet.verification: Free Browser API zone starts without card. Robots.txt exceptions require KYC; restricted targets may require compliance permission. Standalone residential proxy network KYC must not be assumed mandatory for ordinary Browser API signup.
fleet.tiers: Pricing advertises unlimited concurrent Browser API sessions on PAYG/scaled plans.
fleet.notes: No numeric new-account concurrency cap or quota-increase SLA in inspected docs; null retains advertised-unlimited/unknown distinction. Traffic credits and compliance gates can prevent practical fleet use independently of concurrency. Each session is limited to one target domain (navigate_domains_limit), so agents browsing across sites need a new session per domain.

snapshot_auto.quote: Browser API session can last up to 60 minutes. Once the maximum session time is reached the session will automatically timeout.
snapshot_auto.note: Sessions are ephemeral remote Chromium instances (5-min idle timeout, 60-min max) that simply end; no state save/restore documented. The only 'session persistence' is reusing the same proxy peer/IP via CDP Proxy.useSession, not a browser/machine snapshot.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Use this command to reuse the same proxy peer across multiple browsing sessions.
snapshot_on_demand.note: No snapshot/checkpoint/profile-save API in the Browser API docs; the closest feature (Proxy.useSession) only pins the exit IP. Marketing page says it maintains 'consistent IPs and browser state between sessions' but the docs only describe the proxy peer.

harness_api.quote: Currently, the only way to connect to Browser API is via WebSocket or HTTPS endpoints using your zone credentials (username and password). There is no REST API connection method at this time.
harness_api.note: Remote browser driven over CDP/WebDriver (Puppeteer, Playwright, Selenium); no agent harness runs inside. Bright Data also sells a separate 'Agent Browser' product and an MCP server that let an outside agent drive browsers; neither is an in-sandbox harness API.

guest_firewall.quote: Currently, the only way to connect to Browser API is via WebSocket or HTTPS endpoints using your zone credentials (username and password).
guest_firewall.note: Managed browser only; no shell/root/OS access, so no in-guest nftables/iptables.

secret_proxy.quote: Browser API is configured by default to prevent any attempts to log in to accounts by disabling password entry.
secret_proxy.note: No credential-injection proxy or secret store. Logins are blocked by default (exception needs KYC + compliance approval). Client TLS certificates can be pushed into a session via CDP Browser.addCertificate (removed at session end) - the secret enters the browser, so it is not a secret proxy.

volume_attach.quote:
File Downloads
CSV, PDF, binary files via CDP
volume_attach.note: No filesystem or volumes exposed; files only come out via CDP download commands. No volume concept in docs.

volume_shared.note: No volume/storage concept for Browser API sessions.
